claims.text: An integrated CALPHAD and DFT framework can accurately and efficiently predict melting and liquid-phase properties across NiFeCoCr-based high-entropy alloys.
The target materials are homogeneous, as-cast NiFeCoCr-based high-entropy alloys.
Pd additions can tune phase behavior in the NiFeCoCr alloy family.
Experimental calibration can make a combined CALPHAD and DFT approach applicable over a compositional range.
The framework is intended for equilibrium conditions near the melting point.
High configurational entropy stabilizes a homogenized solid state before melting.
The approach is limited to compositions with moderate non-ideal mixing.
Pd addition and heat treatment reduce the distribution of magnetic exchange energies and produce more magnetically homogeneous NiFeCoCrPdx alloys.
Atomic-species distribution and exchange energies mediate melting and influence fusion properties.
CALPHAD supplies thermodynamic consistency while DFT supplies electronic-structure detail.
Combining CALPHAD and DFT captures both enthalpic and entropic contributions to phase transitions.
Configurational entropy minimizes compositional fluctuations in high-entropy alloys.
Minor Pd additions can systematically tune melting properties while reducing uncertainty in the predicted energy landscape.
Melting temperature, fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, and volume change at melting will be predicted within approximately ±5% of experiment for NiFeCoCr-based alloys.
Liquid density and heat capacity will be predicted within approximately ±5% for compositions that approximate ideal mixing.
Current approaches require extensive experiments or separate modeling strategies and often have uncertain, poorly transferable predictions.
The approach should perform best for predominantly transition-metal high-entropy alloys in which electronic interactions and configurational entropy dominate.
Strong non-ideal mixing or formation of intermetallic compounds will limit the approach's applicability.
Non-ideal liquid mixing and high-temperature vibrational anharmonicity may increase prediction errors outside the calibrated composition range.
Systematic errors greater than ±10% for multiple properties across the compositional series would falsify the proposed predictive framework.
